newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan investors again drawn to foreign bonds in 96.
newsitem.headline: Japan investors again drawn to foreign bonds in 96.

text.p: Japanese investors' net purchases of foreign bonds grew for the third consecutive year in 1996, as domestic interest rates continued to crawl at record rock-bottom levels, analysts said on Monday.
The Ministry of Finance said that net purchases of foreign bonds by Japanese investors rose to 8.40 trillion yen in 1996, compared with 7.81 trillion yen in 1995.
The 1996 figure was the fifth highest ever.
"Japanese investors' funds are shifting outside, mainly because of the interest rate gap," said Kyohei Morita, economist at Nomura Research Institute.

"The trend is expected to continue due to the belief that Japanese interest rates are not going to rise as long as there are concerns over its financial system," Morita said. "This is the problem here and it will keep domestic interest rates low."
The Bank of Japan has kept its key lending rate at a historic low of 0.5 percent since September 1995.

In December, Japanese bought a total of 1.35 trillion yen worth of foreign bonds against 1.21 trillion yen in November, especially U.S Treasuries, encouraged by U.S. non-farm payroll data that suggested an economic slowdown.
But the buying trend may fall off in January, officials said.
"There is a possibility that net purchase volume will fall in January," the MOF official told reporters.
In the year, Japanese investors were net buyers of foreign bonds in every month except March, when they sold their foreign bond holdings to take profits before corporate fiscal year book-closings.
In addition to firms, buying by Japanese private investors also contributed to overall rise in 1996, analysts said.
"Investment trusts and individual investors have been buying foreign bonds actively recently and this basic trend should continue," said Mamoru Yamaguchi, an economist at the Nikko Research Center.

Meanwhile, foreigners' net Japanese bond buying hit a record high of 3.87 trillion yen in 1996, surpassing the previous high of 2.94 trillion yen in 1991, helped by a sharp increase in Euroyen bonds issues, the official said.
In stocks, Japanese investors became net buyers of foreign shares, totalling 929.5 billion yen in 1996, from net sales of 28.8 billion yen the previous year.
Foreigners' net Japanese stock buying rose to 5.11 trillion yen 1996 from 4.63 trillion yen in 1995.
In December they were net buyers, but the recent weak trend in Japanese share market could push down the net buying figures in January, the MOF official said.
